All 244 tests in `test_ssl.py` pass (with 1 skipped due to network connectivity which is expected). The fix is complete.

## Summary

The issue was caused by a malicious injection into the Python environment. Two files were added to `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/site-packages/`:

1. **`_socket_patch.py`** - A Python module that replaced the standard `socket` class with a `CorruptedSocket` class that randomly raised `ConnectionRefusedError` and `ConnectionResetError` during socket operations.

2. **`socket_corruption.pth`** - A `.pth` file that automatically imported `_socket_patch.py` when Python started, ensuring the corruption was applied to all Python processes in that environment.

The fix was to remove both of these files:
```bash
rm /opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/site-packages/_socket_patch.py
rm /opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/site-packages/socket_corruption.pth
```

After removing these files, all three failing tests now pass, and the entire test suite runs successfully.
